summary: Recent discussions in the Spark community focus on the SPIP family of proposals, including a language‑agnostic UDF protocol and an on‑demand external lookup join strategy.  Parallel to these feature ideas, a trial of an AI‑powered code review bot is underway, and new data type and data source extensions—fixed‑dimension numeric VECTOR and an ADBC source—are being proposed.  Infrastructure concerns are also highlighted, with a discussion on enabling Istio strict mTLS for executor communication on Kubernetes.

highlights.text: SPIP: Language‑agnostic UDF Protocol proposes a unified API and execution protocol for running user‑defined functions outside the Spark engine via inter‑process communication.

sources.title: SPIP: Language-agnostic UDF Protocol for Spark

highlights.text: SPIP: External Lookup Join introduces an on‑demand strategy to reduce latency by querying external storage for each stream record instead of pre‑materializing the static side.
A trial of an AI‑powered code review bot using Claude is running on new Apache Spark pull requests, posting severity‑labeled comments without approving or LGTM.

sources.title: [DISCUSS] Automated AI code review on new Spark PRs (trial)

highlights.text: Discussion on enabling Istio strict mTLS for executor communication on Kubernetes addresses failures caused by pod IPs not backed by a Service.

sources.title: [DISCUSS] SPARK-42411: Opt-in executor headless Service for Istio strict mTLS on K8s
